name: Election Interference and Countering the "Orange Revolution" (2004) (C0096)

techniques.comment: The conduct of an aggressive information campaign in favor of "their" candidate with the direct participation of the head of the Russian state: live on three Ukrainian television channels two weeks before the vote, praise was voiced for the candidate's government - "V. Yanukovych's government achieved more: they managed to fill this growth with good quality. That is, Ukraine's economy is developing in a diversified way"(Citation: Прямая линия с жителями Украины 2004). In parallel, opponents were demonized with accusations of nationalism and pro-fascist views.

An attempt to physically eliminate the leader of the democratic opposition V. Yushchenko at the height of the election campaign by dioxin poisoning: in late December 2004 "a patient presented with TCDD poisoning; the levels in his blood serum (108000 pg/g lipid weight) were more than 50 000-fold greater than those in the general population"(Citation: TCDD poisoning in Victor Yushchenko (The Lancet) 2009). The poisoning led to severe disfigurement of the candidate's face.

The instigation of the threat of splitting the country in response to the protests: at the congress in Sievierodonetsk on November 28, 2004, Regions faction leader R. Bohatyriova gave a direct promise of a separatist referendum - "we will not go to it with you, we will hold a referendum on the creation of a South-Eastern state (ovation, applause)"(Citation: Стенограмма Северодонецкого съезда 2004). The presence of Russian officials lent this Moscow's sanction: the mayor of Moscow Yu. Luzhkov reminded the hall from the rostrum that "our President of Russia Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin was the first to congratulate Viktor Fedorovych Yanukovych on his victory"(Citation: Стенограмма Северодонецкого съезда 2004).
